target.title: Stabilize Codex Computer Use readiness
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex Computer Use readiness could go stale or look healthy when it was not actually usable. OpenClaw agents can run with isolated per-agent `CODEX_HOME` directories, so one agent could keep a stale cached Computer Use plugin even after the locally installed Codex.app bundle was updated. Status/setup also reported coarse plugin availability without separately proving installation, MCP exposure, and live `list_apps` behavior.

That is how a request could ask for Codex Computer Use while the runtime silently lacked a working Computer Use bridge or fell back to other automation without making the failure inspectable.

## Summary

This PR hardens Codex Computer Use setup so OpenClaw no longer treats “plugin exists somewhere” as sufficient readiness.

It adds:

- shared local bundled Computer Use plugin cache reconciliation for per-agent `CODEX_HOME` directories, defaulting to a symlink back to the locally installed Codex.app bundle and removing stale cached versions
- decomposed `/codex computer-use status` results for installation, MCP exposure, and a live `computer-use.list_apps` probe
- 60s live-probe timeout, exactly one 60s retry, and narrow auto-repair that only terminates stale `SkyComputerUseClient ... mcp` children
- periodic per-shared-client Computer Use health probes on the configured 30/60/120/240 minute cadence, using the same live-probe and repair path
- fail-closed setup behavior by default while keeping browser/DOM fallback available when explicitly requested outside the Computer Use setup path
- config/schema/docs for `liveTestTimeoutMs`, `toolCallTimeoutMs`, `leaseTimeoutMs`, `healthCheckIntervalMinutes`, `pluginCacheMode`, `fallbackOnFailure`, and `autoRepair`
- a window-scope Computer Use lease manager with renewal/preemption semantics for callers that can supply a stable window id
- `openclaw doctor` surfacing for enabled Codex Computer Use, including configured health cadence and the status command to inspect installation/exposure/live-test layers

## Context

This addresses the failure mode where one OpenClaw agent could keep using a stale per-agent Codex plugin cache even after Codex.app had a newer bundled Computer Use plugin, and where status/setup could report only coarse plugin availability instead of separating install state, MCP exposure, and live runtime health.

The previous direction in #96730 improved app-server command selection/startup behavior, but it did not make Computer Use readiness globally inspectable across agents, did not reconcile isolated per-agent plugin caches with the locally installed Codex.app bundle, and did not prove the MCP bridge with a real `list_apps` call before reporting readiness. This PR closes those gaps locally and offline; it does not depend on a remote marketplace.

## Notes

The new lease manager is window-scoped by design, not app-scoped and not host-global. Native Codex MCP notifications are observational, so full pre-execution enforcement requires Computer Use tool payloads to expose a stable window identifier before the MCP call begins. The PR documents that boundary and adds the tested lease primitive for call sites that can provide that scope.

## Evidence

Post-rebase on `origin/main` (`8fa83d2742`), I verified the patch locally with targeted unit coverage, command formatting/doctor coverage, and TypeScript checks:

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex-app-server-support.config.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-health.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-cache.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-leases.test.ts` — 3 files, 8 tests passed
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex-app-server-tools.config.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/request.test.ts` — 2 files, 31 tests passed
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex-app-server-runtime.config.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/config.test.ts` — 1 file, 115 tests passed
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts` — 1 file, 8 tests passed
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/commands/doctor/shared/codex-route-warnings.test.ts extensions/codex/src/commands.test.ts` — 2 files, 244 tests passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`

### Real macOS Codex.app proof (redacted)

After the `a26f850` ephemeral-probe fix, I ran the patched branch's Computer Use install/readiness path against one isolated local Codex.app app-server client. This exercises the same installation, MCP exposure, and live `computer-use.list_apps` layers that `/codex computer-use status` reports, without using a fresh app-server process for each step.

Redacted proof summary:

```json
{
  "proofCommand": "patched branch installCodexComputerUse with one isolated Codex.app app-server client",
  "codexAppServerCommand": "/Applications/Codex.app/Contents/Resources/codex app-server",
  "codexServerVersion": "0.142.5",
  "marketplacePath": "/Applications/Codex.app/Contents/Resources/plugins/openai-bundled/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json",
  "elapsedMs": 6783,
  "ready": true,
  "reason": "ready",
  "installed": true,
  "pluginEnabled": true,
  "mcpServerAvailable": true,
  "pluginName": "computer-use",
  "mcpServerName": "computer-use",
  "marketplaceName": "openai-bundled",
  "installation": {
    "status": "installed",
    "ok": true,
    "message": "Computer Use plugin is installed and enabled."
  },
  "exposure": {
    "status": "available",
    "ok": true,
    "message": "Computer Use MCP server computer-use exposes 10 tools."
  },
  "liveTest": {
    "status": "passed",
    "ok": true,
    "attempted": true,
    "attempts": 1,
    "timeoutMs": 60000,
    "retried": false,
    "repaired": false,
    "durationMs": 5124,
    "message": "Computer Use live test passed."
  },
  "warnings": [],
  "message": "Computer Use is ready.",
  "tools": [
    "click",
    "drag",
    "get_app_state",
    "list_apps",
    "perform_secondary_action",
    "press_key",
    "scroll",
    "select_text",
    "set_value",
    "type_text"
  ]
}
```

The proof run used the branch code after `thread/start` was changed to send `ephemeral: true` for the readiness probe, and the branch test suite includes an assertion for that field in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use.test.ts`.
